bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System relating to "Quality Control Standards for Automated Valuation Models".
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.

industries.rationale: The rule directly regulates mortgage originators and secondary market issuers, which are core banking and financial-sector activities.
The rule governs automated valuation models used to determine real estate values securing mortgages, directly affecting property valuation practices.
The rule sets quality control standards for automated valuation model software and technology used in mortgage lending.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would nullify a federal rule published in August 2024 that requires quality control standards for automated valuation models—computer programs used to estimate property values when issuing or selling mortgages. If enacted, the resolution would eliminate these quality control requirements, leaving automated valuation models without the standards the rule imposed. The resolution uses the Congressional Review Act, which allows Congress to overturn recently issued regulations.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone with a bank account, a loan or savings.

bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Department of Energy relating to "Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Walk-In Coolers and Walk-In Freezers".

industries.rationale: Grocery stores and restaurant chains operate walk-in coolers and freezers and would face different equipment compliance costs depending on whether the standards take effect.
Manufacturers of walk-in coolers, freezers, doors, and refrigeration systems would need to redesign products to meet the new standards or continue current designs if the rule is nullified.
Hotels and large food-service operations use walk-in refrigeration and would be subject to the equipment standards.
Food processing and cold-storage facilities use walk-in refrigeration equipment and would be affected by changes in equipment efficiency requirements.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would block a Department of Energy rule that set stricter energy efficiency standards for walk-in coolers and freezers used in commercial settings. The rule, finalized in December 2024, would have required walk-in refrigeration equipment to meet new energy consumption limits starting in 2027 and 2028. If passed, the resolution would nullify those standards and leave the existing, less stringent requirements in place.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act
bill.latestActionText: Read the second time. Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 10.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates new litigation exposure for federal agencies, affecting federal and state government operations and budgets.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, increasing demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would require the Department of Homeland Security to detain individuals who are in the country without authorization and have been arrested for or charged with burglary, theft, larceny, or shoplifting. It would also allow state governments to sue the federal government for injunctive relief when federal immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing individuals from custody or not fulfilling visa or asylum processing requirements—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

plain.whoItTouches: People applying to live here, and their families here. People applying to come here, and their families here.

bill.title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States requiring a balanced budget for the Federal Government.
bill.latestActionText: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the resolution Failed by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 211 - 207 (Roll no. 95).

industries.rationale: A binding spending cap could constrain defense appropriations unless overridden by supermajority vote or wartime declaration.
Federal health spending (Medicare, Medicaid) represents a large share of the budget and could face constraints under the cap.
Federal pharmaceutical reimbursement and research funding could be affected by overall spending limits.
Federal education grants and student aid could be subject to the spending cap.
Federal infrastructure and public-works spending could be constrained by the cap on total expenditures.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would cap annual federal spending at the average of the previous three years' revenue, adjusted for population and inflation. Exceeding the cap would require a two-thirds vote in both chambers of Congress, or a declaration of war. Any new tax or tax-rate increase would also require a two-thirds vote in both chambers. The rules would take effect five years after ratification.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who pays tax or gets a federal payment.

bill.title: Pharmacists Fight Back [in Federal Employee Health Benefit Plans Act]
bill.latestActionText: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 40 - 2.
subjects: Government employee pay, benefits, personnel management

industries.rationale: Pharmacy benefit managers, which this bill targets with new liability and judicial review, are typically part of or contracted by health insurers managing federal employee drug benefits.
The bill directly affects pharmacists and the terms under which they dispense prescription drugs, altering the contractual and fee structure in the federal employee drug supply chain.
The bill creates new federal civil causes of action and judicial review procedures, which would generate litigation between pharmacists and PBMs.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would allow pharmacists to sue pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) in federal court if they believe PBM fees or contract terms are unfair, and would let courts review and potentially overturn those fees. The bill applies specifically to prescription drug plans offered to federal employees and retirees. It creates a new legal pathway for pharmacists to challenge the business practices of the middlemen who manage drug benefits.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who fills a prescription. Anyone who pays a medical bill.

bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "National Primary Drinking Water Regulations for Lead and Copper: Improvements (LCRI)".
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

industries.rationale: Water utilities would be directly relieved of the 10-year mandate to replace lead and galvanized service lines if this resolution passes.
Contractors and engineering firms would lose anticipated work from the mandated service line replacement program if the rule is nullified.
Manufacturers of water pipes, fittings, and related infrastructure materials would see reduced demand if the replacement mandate does not proceed.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would block an Environmental Protection Agency rule issued in October 2024 that requires water systems to replace all lead and certain galvanized service lines within 10 years. The EPA rule was designed to reduce lead exposure in drinking water under the Safe Drinking Water Act. If this resolution passes, the EPA rule would be nullified and those replacement requirements would not take effect.

bill.title: No Taxpayer Funding for Abortion and Abortion Insurance Full Disclosure Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

industries.rationale: The bill directly restricts what health insurance plans may cover and how federal subsidies interact with abortion coverage in qualified health plans.
The bill prohibits federal health care facilities and federal employees from providing abortion services, affecting facilities that currently receive federal funds.
Organizations focused on reproductive health policy and abortion access or restrictions have a direct stake in the regulatory framework this bill establishes.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would make permanent the restrictions on federal funding for abortion services and health insurance coverage that includes abortion. Currently, these restrictions are renewed each year through appropriations bills; the bill would apply them across all federal programs and funds. It would also prohibit qualified health plans offered through insurance marketplaces from covering abortion. The bill includes exceptions for cases of rape, incest, or when the pregnant person's life is in danger.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys health insurance. Anyone who pays a medical bill.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects manufacturers of consumer appliances and commercial equipment subject to the certification, labeling, and enforcement requirements being nullified.
Retailers selling covered appliances would be affected by changes to labeling requirements and product classification rules.
Energy efficiency standards and their enforcement affect the market for energy-saving technologies and services.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would block a Department of Energy rule published in October 2024 that updated certification, labeling, and enforcement requirements for energy efficiency standards on consumer appliances like washing machines and dishwashers, as well as commercial equipment such as computer room air conditioners. The rule was intended to align reporting with current energy conservation standards and help the Department classify products correctly. If passed, the resolution would nullify these updated requirements.

bill.title: SAVE Moms and Babies Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
subjects: Drug safety, medical device, and laboratory regulation

industries.rationale: The bill directly prohibits approval of new abortion drugs and imposes significant new regulatory restrictions on already-approved drugs in this category.
The bill creates new certification requirements for prescribing practitioners and mandates they have surgical intervention capability, changing practice obligations.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit the FDA from approving any new drugs intended to terminate pregnancy. For drugs already approved for this purpose, it would impose new restrictions: requiring in-person dispensing by a specially certified practitioner, prohibiting use after 70 days of gestation, and mandating that the practitioner be able to provide surgical intervention. The bill would also prevent practitioners from both prescribing and dispensing these medications.
